state.decision: How the Editor and engine should store a path vertex's kind (corner, smooth, symmetric, auto) and derive the handles of an auto vertex.
state.what_exists_today: BezierPath stores only the handles as offsets. The Editor infers smooth when a vertex has two opposite handles and corner otherwise; it cannot tell smooth from symmetric, and there is no auto vertex. Dragging a handle of a smooth vertex keeps the other handle's length; Alt breaks it. Every renderer reads the stored handles as they are.
state.requirements_from_the_specs: Pen spec v2 sections 4 and 6: a stored kind per anchor; for auto, store the mode and tension and DERIVE the handles at evaluation, materialising them only on conversion to a manual mode; never silently overwrite hand edits; smooth keeps the other handle collinear and opposite with its own length, symmetric mirrors it.

options.A: An optional parallel list vertex_kinds on BezierPath (absent on old scenes), with an optional auto tension; an auto vertex's stored handles are ignored and derived (centripetal Catmull-Rom from its neighbours) by one function used by every consumer of the path (renderer, bounds, hit tests).
options.B: No stored kind: keep inferring from handles; auto is an Editor action that writes manual handles once.
options.C: Store the kind in a separate side table keyed by object and vertex index, outside the path.

best_storage.instructions: Which storage should GrapiX adopt for the vertex kind?

criteria.A: Option A: an optional vertex_kinds list on the path, handles of auto vertices derived by one shared function.
criteria.B: Option B: no stored kind, infer from handles, auto writes manual handles once.
criteria.C: Option C: a side table outside the path.

derive_in_one_place.instructions: Must the derivation of an auto vertex's handles live in one function that every consumer (render preparation, bounds, hit testing, export) calls, so editor and playout cannot disagree?

criteria.false: No: each consumer may derive them its own way.

auto_never_overwrites_hand_edits.instructions: When the author drags a handle of an auto vertex, should the vertex first become a manual smooth vertex with the derived handles written out, so a hand edit is never lost to re-derivation?

criteria.true: Yes: materialise then edit; the author's work is never silently overwritten.
criteria.false: No: keep it auto and discard the drag.
